course.title: Natural Hair Care
course.tagline: Care for natural hair properly: washing, moisturising, protective styles and growth.

days.title: Welcome to Natural Hair Care
days.goal: By the end of today you can explain and practise: Your kit is a wide-tooth comb, spray bottle, leave-in, oils, butter and a satin bonnet.

video.title: Curly Hair Routine to GROW, MOISTURIZE, and DEFINE your Natural Hair (all hair types)

steps: Get your tools ready: wide-tooth comb, leave-in conditioner and satin bonnet.
Watch the video. It explains the main point in simple steps: A satin bonnet protects natural hair from breakage at night.
Your kit is a wide-tooth comb, spray bottle, leave-in, oils, butter and a satin bonnet. Go slowly. Practise on a model or a practice head.
Do the same move three times. Check your work in a mirror or a photo after each try.
Write down what went well, what was hard, and one thing to do better tomorrow.
days.task: Practise welcome to natural hair care on a model or a practice head. Your kit is a wide-tooth comb, spray bottle, leave-in, oils, butter and a satin bonnet. Take a photo of your work.

quiz.q: What is the key point of today's lesson on welcome to natural hair care?
options: You should rush through the technique to save time.
A satin bonnet protects natural hair from breakage at night.
The best result comes from skipping the preparation step.
You never need to check your work until the very end.
quiz.explain: A satin bonnet protects natural hair from breakage at night.

quiz.q: Which tool is most essential for welcome to natural hair care?
options: clipper with guards
trimmer
wide-tooth comb
foil shaver
quiz.explain: The wide-tooth comb is the essential tool for this work.

quiz.q: What should you always do when working on welcome to natural hair care?
options: disinfect your clippers between clients
never cut broken skin
check the client for cuts before starting
detangle gently from the ends upward

days.title: Porosity Explained
days.goal: By the end of today you can explain and practise: Test porosity with a strand in water: floating means low porosity, sinking means high.

video.title: How can I tell my hair's level of porosity?

steps: Get your tools ready: wide-tooth comb, leave-in conditioner and satin bonnet.
Watch the video. It explains the main point in simple steps: Low porosity hair floats in water and resists moisture.
Test how well hair soaks up water: put one strand in water. If it floats, the hair takes in very little water, sinking means high. Go slowly. Practise on a model or a practice head.
Do the same move three times. Check your work in a mirror or a photo after each try.
Write down what went well, what was hard, and one thing to do better tomorrow.
